title: Edge complexity of weighted graphs: involutory symmetries and NP-hardness
summary: The edge complexity of a weighted graph is the smallest ratio of the Fourier $\ell^1$ and $\ell^2$ norms of its adjacency matrix over all vertex labelings. We study the difficulty of finding this minimum by relating it to a graph symmetry. Adding a universal vertex with sufficiently large incident weight produces an explicit Fourier $\ell^1$ lower bound. We show that equality holds exactly when the source graph has a fixed-point-free involutory automorphism.
